item.title: Exploring Sociocultural Interactions and Influences Shaping Clinical Education | Published in Australian Journal of Clinical Education
item.description: By Nastassia Timothy, Shamila Manie & 1 more. This study explores how sociocultural factors impact physiotherapy students

item.title: Clinical Competency Paused: The New Graduate Nurse Experience of Transition Post COVID-19. What Was the Effectiveness of Nurse Education Programmes in Developing Clinical Competency Among Newly Qualified Nurses in New Zealand During the COVID-19 Pandemic? | Published in Australian Journal of Clinical Education
item.description: By Karla Breen Rickerby. This integrative review aims to identify and synthesize the current position and identify the longer-term impact of COVID-19 on the nurse education system in New Zealand.

item.title: Simulation-Based Learning for Pain Medicine: A Scoping Review of Undergraduate Education | Published in Australian Journal of Clinical Education
item.description: By Alina Savastyuk, Carlos Campos & 1 more. Simulation-based education improves undergraduate medical students

item.title: To Fall at the Final Hurdle? Unpacking Experiences of Ophthalmology Trainees Undertaking Final Summative Examinations in Australia and New Zealand | Published in Australian Journal of Clinical Education
item.description: By Belinda Jessup, Penny Allen & 5 more. Passing final summative examination in ophthalmology may be challenging due to ambiguous questions, specialist knowledge demands, and time pressures. Addressing examination reliability across semesters could support ophthalmology trainee achievement.

item.title: Evaluating Clinical Placement Performance in Allied Health Student-Led Healthcare Services: A Modified Delphi Study | Published in Australian Journal of Clinical Education
item.description: By Lisa Simmons, Ruth Barker & 2 more. This study establishes 44 expert-identified measures for evaluating allied health clinical placement performance, aiming to improve consistency, support educational outcomes, and guide future research and policy in health professional education.

item.title: Client Experiences, Perceptions and Acceptability of a Digital Health Enabled Student-Led Exercise Physiology Clinic for Metabolic Conditions: A Qualitative Study | Published in Australian Journal of Clinical Education
item.description: By Riley C C Brown, Sophie Marron & 5 more. Evaluating client perspectives on student-led digital health clinics reveals insights to enhance accessibility, technology use, and overall satisfaction in exercise physiology services.

item.title: Preparing Physiotherapy Students for Caseload Management in Clinical Practice Placements: Perspectives of Students and Clinical Educators | Published in Australian Journal of Clinical Education
item.description: By Elaine McGivern, Allison Mandrusiak & 2 more. Clinical placements offer physiotherapy students varied exposure to caseload management. This study highlights clinical educator influence, challenges, and the need for equitable learning to strengthen new graduate readiness for practice.

item.title: Prioritising the Pipeline: Updating Undergraduate Medical Genetics Education to Support the Future of Genomic Medicine in Australia | Published in Australian Journal of Clinical Education
item.description: By Kelsey Walsh. This review identifies deficiencies in genetics education for Australian medical students, examines global approaches, and suggests a competency-based framework to prepare future doctors for genomic medicine.

item.title: The Influences Shaping New Graduate Occupational Therapists’ Experiences of Learning to Make Paediatric Intervention Decisions in Non-Government Organisations: A Case Study Analysis | Published in Australian Journal of Clinical Education
item.description: By Elizabeth Moir, Jodie Copley & 1 more. NDIS funding constraints limit new graduates’ access to supervision and support within non-government organisations. Structured, context-sensitive support is essential to develop competent clinical decision-making and ensure high-quality paediatric service delivery.

item.title: Using a Novel 3D-Printed Foot Model in Simulation-Based Learning of Podiatry Clinical Skills: A Qualitative Study on Students
item.description: By Julie Nguyen, Adriaan Erasmus & 1 more. A novel 3D-printed foot model enhanced podiatry students’ confidence and safety in scalpel skills training, offering a superior learning experience compared to a commercial model in simulation-based education.
